```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230803)
set.seed(20230803)
```

Kim et al. (2023) modelled the natural history of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
(DMD) in ambulatory boys from the ImagingDMD study. Two endpoints were modelled
jointly: the 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), the usual primary endpoint of
ambulatory DMD trials, and the fat fraction of a lower-limb muscle measured by
MR spectroscopy. The paper fitted two multivariate models, one pairing 6MWD
with the vastus lateralis fat fraction (FFVL) and one pairing it with the
soleus fat fraction (FFSOL). The package ships them as two model files that
share this vignette:

```{r load_models}
mod_vl <- rxode2::rxode2(nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Kim_2023_DMD_6MWD_FFVL"))
mod_sol <- rxode2::rxode2(nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Kim_2023_DMD_6MWD_FFSOL"))
```

Reference: Kim S, Willcocks RJ, Daniels MJ, Morales JF, Yoon DY, Triplett WT,
Barnard AM, Senesac CR, Lott DJ, Forbes SC, Walter GA, Sweeney HL, Vandenborne
K (2023). Multivariate modeling of magnetic resonance biomarkers and clinical
outcome measures for Duchenne muscular dystrophy clinical trials. *CPT
Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol* 12(10):1437-1449.
[doi:10.1002/psp4.13021](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13021)

There is no drug in these models. The model time is the boy's **age in
years**, so a simulation data set carries age in its `time` column, has no
dosing rows, and supplies four time-fixed baseline covariates:

| Column | Meaning | Units |
|---|---|---|
| `WALK_DIST_BL` | the boy's own 6MWD at the baseline visit | m |
| `FF_VL_BL` / `FF_SOL_BL` | the boy's own vastus lateralis / soleus fat fraction at baseline | fraction 0-1 |
| `AGE_BASE` | age at the baseline visit; below 7 years selects the "young" covariate exponents | years |
| `CONMED_STEROID` | corticosteroid use at baseline (1 = yes) | binary |

## Population

The analysis data set held 118 boys with DMD aged 5-20 years at assessment,
with 567 observations of each of 6MWD, FFVL and FFSOL (Kim 2023 Results "Data
summary"). Boys were ambulatory at the derived baseline visit, the first visit
at which all three measures were available; baseline ages were 5-13 years.
Boys taking experimental dystrophin-restoring therapies, boys likely to express
dystrophin (milder, Becker-like mutations) and boys still walking after age 15
were excluded. By the 7-year baseline-age cut-off and steroid use, the cohort
split into 10 young and 8 old boys without steroids and 27 young and 73 old
boys on steroids (Figure 2f). 6MWD values missing because a boy could no longer
walk were treated as censored (M4 method). The data came from three US sites
(University of Florida, Oregon Health & Science University, Children's Hospital
of Philadelphia) with annual assessments over 1-9 years.

```{r population}
str(mod_vl$population)
```

## Model structure

For boy *i* at age *Age* (Kim 2023 Equations 4 and 5):

- 6MWD = S0_6MWD x (1 - DPmax_6MWD x Age^g / (DPT50^g + Age^g)), with
  DPmax_6MWD fixed to 1, so the walk distance falls from its early-childhood
  level S0_6MWD to zero along a very steep sigmoid (Hill coefficient about 53).
- FF = S0_FF + DPmax_FF x Age^g / (DPT50^g + Age^g): the fat fraction rises
  from S0_FF by at most DPmax_FF. DPmax_FF is logit-normal, on (0, 1) for FFVL
  and on (0, 2) for FFSOL (Supplement 2 `max=2`).

All other parameters are log-normal (Equation 2). Covariates enter as power
terms of the baseline scores centred on group medians and as exp(beta) for
steroid use (Equation 3). Every baseline-score effect has a separate exponent
and centring value for boys younger and older than 7 years at baseline; the
centring values are printed only in Supplement 2. The two endpoints are linked
by correlated random effects on the ages at half-maximal change of 6MWD and of
the fat fraction and on the 6MWD intercept. The residual error is proportional
for 6MWD and Monolix `combined1` for the fat fraction.

## Source trace

| Element | Source location | Model file |
|---|---|---|
| 6MWD sigmoid Imax, DPmax fixed 1 | Equation 4; Table 1; Supplement 2 `Imax_pop` FIXED | both |
| Fat-fraction sigmoid Emax | Equation 5; Table 1 | both |
| Logit-normal DPmax_FF on (0, 1) / (0, 2) | Equation 1; Supplement 2 `Emax` definitions | FFVL / FFSOL |
| Power and exponential covariate model | Equation 3; Table 1 betas | both |
| Young / old split at a baseline age of 7 years | Methods "Time metric, dependent variables, and covariates" | both |
| Covariate centring values (363, 367, 364 m; 0.04, 0.17, 0.06, 0.09) | Supplement 2 `[COVARIATE]` EQUATION blocks | both |
| Covariate-to-parameter mapping | Supplement 2 `[INDIVIDUAL]` DEFINITION blocks | both |
| Typical values, betas, omegas, correlations, residual SDs | Table 1, one column per model | both |
| Proportional 6MWD and combined1 fat-fraction residual error | Results "Univariate models"; Supplement 2 `[LONGITUDINAL]` | both |
| Simulation covariate profiles | Supplement 3 Table S5 | vignette |

The parameter-level trace is in the trailing comment of every `ini()` line of
the two model files.

## Structural verification

The typical-value solution must equal Equations 4 and 5 evaluated directly.
This compares the solver against the paper's closed form with the same
parameters, so the bound is tight.

```{r closed_form}
ages <- c(0.5, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 18)
cov_vl <- data.frame(
  WALK_DIST_BL = 330, FF_VL_BL = 0.12, AGE_BASE = 8, CONMED_STEROID = 1
)
ev_vl <- data.frame(id = 1, time = ages, cov_vl)
typ_vl <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vl), ev_vl) |> as.data.frame()

p <- mod_vl$theta
s0w <- exp(p[["le0_walk_dist"]]) *
  (0.12 / 0.17)^p[["e_ff_vl_bl_old_e0_walk_dist"]] *
  (330 / 367)^p[["e_walk_dist_bl_old_e0_walk_dist"]]
t50w <- exp(p[["lt50max_walk_dist"]]) *
  exp(p[["e_conmed_steroid_t50max_walk_dist"]]) *
  (0.12 / 0.17)^p[["e_ff_vl_bl_old_t50max_walk_dist"]]
gw <- exp(p[["lhill_walk_dist"]]) *
  (0.12 / 0.17)^p[["e_ff_vl_bl_old_hill_walk_dist"]]
t50f <- exp(p[["lt50max_ff_vl"]]) *
  (0.12 / 0.17)^p[["e_ff_vl_bl_old_t50max_ff_vl"]]
gf <- exp(p[["lhill_ff_vl"]])
walk_cf <- s0w * (1 - ages^gw / (t50w^gw + ages^gw))
ff_cf <- exp(p[["le0_ff_vl"]]) +
  plogis(p[["logitemax_ff_vl"]]) * ages^gf / (t50f^gf + ages^gf)

stopifnot(
  max(abs(typ_vl$walk_dist - walk_cf)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(typ_vl$ff_vl - ff_cf)) < 1e-9
)
data.frame(age = ages, walk_dist = typ_vl$walk_dist, ff_vl = typ_vl$ff_vl)
```

For the soleus model the young-group 6MWD effect on DPmax_FF acts on the logit
of DPmax_FF / 2, and DPmax_FF stays below its bound of 2 for any baseline:

```{r emax_bound}
ev_sol_young <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4, time = 20,
  WALK_DIST_BL = c(150, 300, 363, 500), FF_SOL_BL = 0.06,
  AGE_BASE = 6, CONMED_STEROID = 0
)
# zeroRe() removes every omega, so rxSolve() warns that a multi-subject
# solve has none; each row here is a typical subject by design.
typ_sol_young <- suppressWarnings(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_sol), ev_sol_young)
) |>
  as.data.frame()
p_sol <- mod_sol$theta
emax_cf <- 2 * plogis(
  p_sol[["logitemax_ff_sol"]] +
    p_sol[["e_walk_dist_bl_young_emax_ff_sol"]] * log(c(150, 300, 363, 500) / 363)
)
stopifnot(
  all(emax_cf > 0 & emax_cf < 2),
  abs(emax_cf[3] - 0.49) < 1e-9
)
data.frame(WALK_DIST_BL = ev_sol_young$WALK_DIST_BL, DPmax_FF = emax_cf)
```

## Published derived quantities

The paper reports that baseline steroid use delays the age at which 6MWD has
fallen by half by about 10%, and delays the corresponding age for FFSOL by a
similar amount (Results "Introducing combined covariates into the model").

```{r steroid_effect}
steroid <- data.frame(
  model = c("6MWD + FFVL", "6MWD + FFSOL", "6MWD + FFSOL"),
  parameter = c("DPT50, 6MWD", "DPT50, 6MWD", "DPT50, FFSOL"),
  delay_factor = c(
    exp(mod_vl$theta[["e_conmed_steroid_t50max_walk_dist"]]),
    exp(mod_sol$theta[["e_conmed_steroid_t50max_walk_dist"]]),
    exp(mod_sol$theta[["e_conmed_steroid_t50max_ff_sol"]])
  )
)
stopifnot(all(steroid$delay_factor > 1.05 & steroid$delay_factor < 1.2))
knitr::kable(steroid, digits = 3)
```

## Simulated trajectories for the Table S5 profiles (Figure 5)

Figure 5 shows the median and the 40th-60th percentile band of 500 simulated
profiles: 50 replicates of 10 boys whose covariate profiles are listed in
Supplement 3 Table S5. All ten boys are in the old baseline-age group. The
profiles are reproduced here with 20 replicates (100 boys per steroid group),
simulating between-subject variability.

```{r table_s5}
s5_vl <- data.frame(
  profile = 1:10,
  WALK_DIST_BL = rep(c(295, 349), 5),
  FF_VL_BL = rep(c(0.17, 0.08), 5),
  CONMED_STEROID = rep(c(0, 1), 5)
)
s5_sol <- data.frame(
  profile = 1:10,
  WALK_DIST_BL = c(295, 349, 216, 295, 349, 216, 295, 349, 216, 295),
  FF_SOL_BL = c(0.11, 0.04, 0.17, 0.11, 0.04, 0.17, 0.11, 0.04, 0.17, 0.11),
  CONMED_STEROID = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0)
)
# Table S5 gives the baseline-age group only ('Old'); any baseline age of
# 7 years or more selects the same exponents.
s5_vl$AGE_BASE <- 9
s5_sol$AGE_BASE <- 9

n_rep <- 20
age_grid <- seq(5, 15, by = 0.25)

make_events <- function(profiles, n_rep, ages) {
  cohort <- profiles[rep(seq_len(nrow(profiles)), n_rep), ]
  cohort$id <- seq_len(nrow(cohort))
  tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = ages) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

sim_vl <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_vl, make_events(s5_vl, n_rep, age_grid),
  keep = "CONMED_STEROID"
) |> as.data.frame()
sim_sol <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_sol, make_events(s5_sol, n_rep, age_grid),
  keep = "CONMED_STEROID"
) |> as.data.frame()

band <- function(sim, var) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::mutate(steroid = ifelse(CONMED_STEROID == 1, "Yes", "No")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(steroid, time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      lo = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.4),
      med = median(.data[[var]]),
      hi = quantile(.data[[var]], 0.6),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

bands <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  band(sim_vl, "walk_dist") |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "(a) 6MWD (m), FFVL model"),
  band(sim_vl, "ff_vl") |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "(b) FFVL"),
  band(sim_sol, "walk_dist") |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "(c) 6MWD (m), FFSOL model"),
  band(sim_sol, "ff_sol") |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "(d) FFSOL")
)
```

```{r figure5, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Kim 2023: median and 40th-60th percentile band of simulated 6MWD and fat fraction for the Table S5 profiles, by steroid use."}
ggplot(bands, aes(time, med, colour = steroid, fill = steroid)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.3, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(No = "#1b2a4a", Yes = "#6ab023")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(No = "#1b2a4a", Yes = "#6ab023")) +
  labs(x = "Age at assessment (years)", y = NULL, colour = "Steroid use", fill = "Steroid use") +
  theme_bw()
```

The medians are compared with values read off Figure 5 by the maintainers.
The early-childhood 6MWD plateau is set almost entirely by S0_6MWD, which has
little variability (omega 0.06), so it is the sharpest test of the
intercepts and the baseline-score effects; the fat fraction at 15 years tests
DPmax_FF and the age sigmoid.

```{r figure5_compare}
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~steroid, ~time, ~published,
  "(a) 6MWD (m), FFVL model", "No", 5, 312,
  "(a) 6MWD (m), FFVL model", "Yes", 5, 348,
  "(b) FFVL", "No", 10, 0.20,
  "(b) FFVL", "Yes", 10, 0.15,
  "(b) FFVL", "No", 15, 0.62,
  "(b) FFVL", "Yes", 15, 0.55,
  "(c) 6MWD (m), FFSOL model", "No", 5, 305,
  "(c) 6MWD (m), FFSOL model", "Yes", 5, 290,
  "(d) FFSOL", "No", 10, 0.165,
  "(d) FFSOL", "Yes", 10, 0.11,
  "(d) FFSOL", "No", 15, 0.51,
  "(d) FFSOL", "Yes", 15, 0.37
)
cmp <- fig5 |>
  dplyr::left_join(bands, by = c("panel", "steroid", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (med - published) / published)

stopifnot(
  # The plateau is set by the intercept parameters and baseline scores.
  all(abs(cmp$pct_diff[cmp$time == 5]) < 6),
  # Fat-fraction medians at 10 and 15 years: robust to cohort draw.
  abs(median(cmp$pct_diff)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::select(panel, steroid, time, published, med, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Panel = panel, `Steroid use` = steroid, `Age (years)` = time,
    `Figure 5 median` = published, `Simulated median` = med,
    `Difference (%)` = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The largest difference, FFVL at 10 years without steroids, falls on the
steepest part of the curve, where a small error in reading the figure moves
the value most.

The 6MWD panels of Figure 5 level off at about 10 m rather than reaching zero.
The model itself has no floor (DPmax_6MWD is 1): values below the walking
limit were censored in the fit, and the published simulation appears to have
been plotted at that limit. The steep 6MWD decline is therefore compared
through the age at which the median falls below 150 m. In the simulation,
steroid use delays that age by about 1.5 years in both models; in Figure 5,
whose curves are drawn through whole-year ages, the delay is about one year.

```{r loss_of_ambulation}
loa <- bands |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("6MWD", panel)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel, steroid) |>
  dplyr::summarise(age_below_150m = min(time[med < 150]), .groups = "drop")
loa_delay <- loa |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = steroid, values_from = age_below_150m) |>
  dplyr::mutate(delay = Yes - No)
stopifnot(all(loa_delay$delay > 0.5 & loa_delay$delay < 2.5))
loa_delay |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Panel = panel, `No steroid (years)` = No, `Steroid (years)` = Yes,
    `Delay (years)` = delay
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Baseline-age group

Each baseline score acts through different exponents in boys younger and older
than 7 years at baseline. For the same baseline 6MWD of 300 m, the 6MWD
intercept is lower in the young group because its exponent is larger
(0.89 versus 0.63 in the FFVL model) and its centring value is 363 m rather
than 367 m:

```{r age_group}
ev_age <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, time = 5, WALK_DIST_BL = 300, FF_VL_BL = 0.17,
  AGE_BASE = c(6, 8), CONMED_STEROID = 1
)
# Two typical subjects; see the note on the zeroRe() warning above.
suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vl), ev_age)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = ifelse(AGE_BASE < 7, "young", "old")) |>
  dplyr::select(group, walk_dist, ff_vl)
```

## PKNCA

This is a natural-history disease-progression model with no drug input, so
there is no concentration-time profile for non-compartmental analysis. The
validation above uses the closed-form solution, the published steroid effects
and the paper's own simulation (Figure 5) instead.

## Assumptions and deviations

- **Boundary of the baseline-age groups.** The paper splits boys at a baseline
  age of 7 years without saying which group a boy of exactly 7.0 years joins.
  The models use young = `AGE_BASE < 7`. Supply a baseline age just below 7 to
  force the young group if a source defines the cut-off the other way.
- **Group-specific covariate columns.** Monolix carried each baseline score in
  two columns (for example `BSSMWTYOUNG` and `BSSMWTOLD`), so that only one
  group's effect applies to any boy. The models take a single column per score
  (`WALK_DIST_BL`, `FF_VL_BL`, `FF_SOL_BL`) and select the group's exponent and
  centring value from `AGE_BASE`, which gives the same individual parameters.
- **Values from Table 1; transforms from Supplement 2.** The `<PARAMETER>`
  values in the Supplement 2 Monolix code are the initial values of the run,
  not the final estimates, and are not used. The supplement does supply the
  covariate centring values, the logit-normal bounds of DPmax_FF and the
  covariate-to-parameter mapping, none of which are printed in the paper.
- **Logit-scale covariate on DPmax_FF (FFSOL).** Monolix applies covariate
  effects on the transformed scale, so the young-group baseline-6MWD effect
  (-1.32) is additive on logit(DPmax_FF / 2), not a power term on DPmax_FF.
- **Censoring.** 6MWD values missing because a boy could no longer walk were
  handled as censored (M4) in the fit. The models predict the uncensored
  walk distance, which reaches 0 m; the censoring limit is not part of the
  model.
- **Simulation variability.** Figure 5 includes between-subject variability,
  residual variability and parameter uncertainty. The replication here
  includes between-subject variability only, with 20 rather than 50
  replicates of the Table S5 profiles, and Table S5 gives the baseline-age
  group but not the age, so a baseline age of 9 years was used for every
  profile.
- **Figure 5 values** in the comparison table were read off the published
  figure by the maintainers and carry reading error of a few percent.
